entry.title: Incident: Intermittent performance issues using Slack
entry.summary:
Issue Summary: On Thursday, July 11, 2024, from 12:10 PM PDT to 12:12 PM PDT, a number of users had trouble loading messages in Slack.
Our internal monitoring systems alerted us of the unexpected spike in error rates which prompted our incident response processes to begin. Through our investigation, we determined that a recent data migration caused an unexpected influx of client reloads, which temporarily overwhelmed the database responsible for servicing the affected API calls.
As a result, an automated safety measure temporarily paused traffic until the database returned to a healthy state. Once error rates returned to normal, users were no longer experiencing trouble.

entry.title: Incident: Issues loading threads
entry.summary:
Issue summary: From 7:13 PM PDT on July 2, 2024 to 2:38 PM PDT on July 3, 2024, some users experienced issues loading threads in Slack.
We traced the issue to one of our databases. Repeated API calls related to threads from one org caused the database responsible for storing that thread to become overwhelmed. This overload affected other users accessing the same database, causing congestion, which prevented them from using it effectively and created further unexpected timeouts.
As an immediate mitigation step, we halted all traffic from users using that API call in order to retrieve the thread from the database which allowed our systems to catch-up. Once traffic started flowing at a reasonable rate again, we reinstated the API call for all users and disallowed the thread that initially caused an issue. This resolved the issue for all impacted users.
We've now added additional code to the problematic thread to bypass this particular API so that any unwanted traffic congestion can be mediated.

entry.title: Incident: Issues sending messages to channels
entry.summary:
Issue Summary: On June 24, 2024 from 11:25AM PDT to July 3, 2024 11:30AM PDT, users were unable to post in some channels due to an "Only some people can post" message on iOS as if the channel was made announcement-only. This initially was handled as a bug, however, the issue began to unexpectedly impact more users. Out of an abundance of caution, we promptly activated our incident response processes to expedite our investigation.
We determined this issue was presenting only temporarily for most users and was often resolved by switching channels, clearing app cache, or by force-closing the app and re-launching.
A fix was implemented in version 24.07.10 of the iOS app to restore channel posting functionality, resolving the issue for affected users. Updating the app is recommended in order to capture the fix.

entry.title: TS-2024-009
entry.summary: Description: Potential for API credential disclosure over plaintext HTTP What happened? The Tailscale API is primarily accessible over TLS-encrypted HTTP at api.tailscale.com. It also has a limited plaintext HTTP handler to serve HTTP to HTTPS redirects. Browsers that connect over plaintext HTTP do not send cookies marked as Secure to prevent them from being disclosed to network intermediaries. However, API clients that connect using plaintext HTTP and send requests with authentication tokens in headers have no such protections to prevent disclosure. Before June 26, 2024, the Tailscale API did not reject credentialed plaintext API requests and instead served them HTTP 302 redirects as it would to browsers. Typical HTTP client libraries handle redirects transparently, and consequently, the user would not necessarily know their credentials had been exposed. Starting on June 26, 2024, the Tailscale API now returns errors for all plaintext HTTP requests that include credentials. Additionally, the Tailscale API now automatically revokes API keys that it observes sent over HTTP and notifies Tailnet security owners of this action. Who was affected? Any Tailscale API client that connected over plaintext HTTP using credentials before June 26, 2024. What was the impact? API clients that connected over plaintext HTTP before June 26, 2024 would have exposed their credentials to network intermediaries, risking them to theft and replay. What do I need to do? No action is needed at this time. Credits Thanks to Joachim Viide for reporting this issue.

entry.title: Incident: Some users unable to connect to Slack
entry.summary:
Issue summary: On June 20, 2024 from 11:30 AM PDT to 11:50 AM PDT, some users were unable to load Slack and may have experienced a “We are unable to load your workspace” error message.
We made a backend update to one of our databases which unexpectedly caused that database to become overloaded, resulting in some users being unable to load Slack. We paused the update until error rates returned to normal, which resolved the issues for all affected users.

entry.title: Incident: Video clips recorded on desktop fail to play on mobile
entry.summary:
Issue summary: On June 18, 2024 from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM PDT, some users had trouble playing video clips on mobile.
Through investigation, we discovered a recent change to how recorded clips were stored when sent on desktop was causing compatibility issues when users attempted to play them on their mobile devices. Though, this change did not affect other file or media types.
We rolled out a fix which allowed these video files to save properly and play on mobile again.

entry.title: Incident with Copilot Pull Request Summaries
entry.summary:
Jun 19, 12:53 UTC Resolved - Between June 18th, 2024 at 09:34 PM UTC and June 19th, 2024 at 12:53 PM the Copilot Pull Request Summaries Service was unavailable. This was due to an internal change in access approach from the Copilot Pull Request service to the Copilot API. We mitigated the incident by reverting the change in access which immediately resolved the errors. We are working to improve our monitoring in this area and reduce our time to detection to more quickly address issues like this one in the future.
Jun 19, 12:31 UTC Update - We are deploying a fix now and expect recovery within the hour. Jun 19, 11:59 UTC Update - We’ve identified an issue with Copilot pull request summaries that has caused errors when attempting to generate summaries since yesterday (June 18, 2024) at around 21:00 UTC. We have identified a fix, and we expect the issue to be resolved within two hours. Jun 19, 11:58 UTC Investigating - We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Copilot

entry.title: Incident: Some users may be unable to complete ownership transfers
entry.summary:
Issue summary: From June 17, 2024, around 9:00 AM until 4:14 PM PDT, users experienced unexpected behaviors that prevented them from completing certain administrative actions, such as transferring workspace ownership, updating workspace retention settings, or reinstalling apps from the Slack App Directory.
We traced this back to an issue with our webpage UI code that prevented certain web elements from appearing or loading properly. These elements would prevent the action from completing. The problematic code was identified and we rolled out a fix to restore the full functionality of these pages.

entry.title: Incident: Some customers may be having issues signing in from external sites
entry.summary:
Issue summary: From 04:50 PM PDT until 06:54 PM PDT on 14 June 2024, some customers using "Sign In With Slack" services through external sites reported connectivity issues. The sign-in pages were not loading correctly and were spinning indefinitely.
A change that was recently released was the root issue. We reverted said change, allowing those affected to be able to sign in via 'Sign In With Slack' services through other sites again.
We apologise for any inconvenience caused.
